question.problem: Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y={x}^{2}+2x+1$ whose tangent has a slope of $-2.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{2}+2x+1.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+2x+1) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\  & =2x+2\cdot 1+0 \\  & =2x+2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=-2$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+2 & =-2 \\ 2x & =-2-2 \\ 2x & =-4 \\ x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $-2$ at the point where $x=-2.$
